problem: Let $F(x)=3{x}^{2}-2x$ for $x\in [0,5),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **odd** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-5,5).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-5,0)?$
worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,5),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,5), \\ -F(-x), & x\in (-5,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-5,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-(3(-x)^{2}-2(-x)) \\  & =-(3{x}^{2}+2x) \\  & =-3{x}^{2}-2x.\end{aligned}
$$
